title: Latency-first tail-trimmer hybrid bucketer for microbatch shaping
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement a latency-prioritized hybrid bucketing strategy that trims low-value tail tokens and groups requests into kernel-aware buckets to reduce wasted padding and optimize kernel selection. Unlike existing length-only binners, this feature combines: 1) tail-trimming heuristics that detect low-attention tail tokens at prefill time; 2) an entropy-aware bucketer that forms buckets by effective compute length (post-trim) and attention profile; 3) a scheduler that biases prefill and small-decode requests onto low-latency kernels and time-slices large decodes to avoid blocking. Expected outcomes: lower p50/p95 latency for latency-sensitive routes, 10-20% reduction in aggregate padded tokens, and improved kernel utilization across GPUs.
motivation: Observed customer routes (chat-short and assistant-snippets) suffer from artificially inflated padding due to long tails and mixed-length traffic in the coalescer. Current bucketizers only use raw sequence length which misses opportunities to safely trim trailing tokens (boilerplate signatures, repeated punctuation) and to match requests to kernels that favor short vs long sequence compute. This work surfaces those opportunities into routing and kernel hints so runtime can make better trade-offs between latency and throughput.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark showing >=10% reduction in padded tokens on mixed-length workload (internal synthetic trace)
P50 latency improvement >=12% on latency-sensitive routes in staging with same throughput
No regressions in model quality measured via automated prompt set (max 0.5% change in BLEU/ROUGE/target metric) after trimming heuristics
Scheduler integrates with kernel-hint API and falls back to baseline kernel when hint unavailable
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout via canary by route
implementation_notes: Add tail-trim pass to prefill analyzer: compute tail-token score using attention-magnitude heuristic and token-repetition detector
Compute effective_length = raw_len - trimmed_tail_length; feed effective_length and attention-variance into bucketer heuristic
Bucketer outputs bucket_id + kernel_hint (short-fast | long-tiling | fused-attn)
Scheduler: prefer short-fast kernels for routes flagged latency-sensitive; if kernel not available, immediately fallback with preemption window to fused-attn to avoid stalling queues
Integrate with existing coalescer to avoid reintroducing padding after bucket assignment; preserve KV cache compatibility by storing original indices and mapping
tradeoffs: Trimming risks minor quality regressions on prompts where tail context is important; mitigated via conservative thresholds and prompt-set QA
Preferring low-latency kernels may reduce overall throughput; will gate policy by route SLA and load signals
Kernel hints increase scheduling complexity and can cause fragmentation of GPU utilization; we will monitor utilization and enable periodic defragmentation runs
experiment_results: Prototype A (conservative trimming): 9% padded-token reduction, 12% p50 improvement on chat-short, quality deltas <0.2%
Prototype B (aggressive trimming): 18% padded-token reduction but BLEU drop 1.1% on synthesis prompts; reverted
Kernel-hint routing: short-fast kernels reduced decode tail latency by 22% for small decodes under 64 tokens; throughput of long-batch decodes unchanged
qa_plan: Create regression suite with 200 representative prompts across routes (latency-sensitive, high-context, code-gen)
Run A/B in staging traffic for 48h with gradual increase: 1% -> 10% -> 50% route traffic
Monitor QoQ metrics: p50/p95 latency, padded tokens per request, token throughput, and quality metrics from eval harness
rollout_plan: Canary rollout per route: enable on non-critical tenant first
Enable conservative trimming threshold globally after 1 week of stable canary
Expose controls in console: trimming aggressiveness slider and kernel routing policy per route
open_questions: What threshold on attention magnitude best separates meaningful vs boilerplate tails? (ML tuning PR required)
Do we extend trimming to user-provided stop sequences or only model-internal tail patterns?
Should dedicated capacity customers be allowed to opt-out of kernel-hint routing for strict throughput guarantees?

next_steps: Triage intermittent preemption race and add deterministic test
Run 48h canary on chat-short route at 5% traffic
Coordinate with PM to add console controls for trimming aggressiveness
review_feedback: PM (Priya Rao): Keep default conservative and surface quality delta per-route before enabling
Design (Marco Liu): UX needs a clear indicator in console when trimming is active for a route
SRE (Nina Patel): Scheduler must expose backpressure signal to autoscaler to avoid OOM spikes
final_notes: This ticket implements a new buckle-between-latency-and-throughput: provide routes opt-in for aggressive latency-first trimming while preserving a safe conservative default. If successful, we will fold parts of the bucketer into the global coalescer as a configurable policy.
